paper.title_en: Boosting the optical depth to Thomson scattering with primordial black hole evaporation at high redshift
paper.abstract_en: BAO and CMB data are somewhat discrepant when interpreted in the context of $Λ$cdm, discrepancies that show up as a `matter density deficit' and as a `CMB lensing excess'. One possible resolution is an increased optical depth to scattering off of free electrons in the post-recombination universe, $τ$, a possibility raised by Sailer et al. 2025 and Jhaveri et al. 2025. Since Planck measurements of the low-$\ell$ polarization `reionization bump' already constrain $τ$ from standard stellar-driven reionization at $z<10$, we investigate additional optical depth sourced by transient or partial reionization at higher redshift from exotic processes. For specificity, we explore the impact of Hawking radiation from a monochromatic spectrum of primordial black holes, retaining the high-$\ell$ $TT/TE/EE$ data that constrain such histories and varying the reionization redshift jointly. We find that the CMB data do not significantly prefer these additional signals: the boost is at most $Δτ\simeq 0.008$, well short of the $Δτ\simeq 0.03$ that would completely eliminate the moderate discrepancy. The matter density deficit and the lensing excess are not significantly eased: we explain why, tracing it to compensation from the reionization redshift and the residual PBH signal at $\ell > 30$.

decision.selection_reason_zh: 论文探讨了通过原初黑洞蒸发增加早期宇宙光学深度以缓解BAO和CMB数据之间的 discrepancies，属于黑洞热力学在天体物理中的应用，理论深度和逻辑清晰，适合推荐。
decision.title_zh: 利用高红移原初黑洞蒸发增强汤姆逊散射的光学深度
decision.abstract_zh: BAO和CMB数据在Λcdm背景下存在一定的不一致，这些不一致表现为“物质密度亏损”和“CMB透镜过剩”。一个可能的解决方案是增加复合后宇宙中自由电子散射的光学深度τ，这是Sailer等人2025年和Jhaveri等人2025年提出的可能性。由于普朗克对低ℓ极化“再电离驼峰”的测量已经从标准恒星驱动的z<10处的再电离约束了τ，我们研究了由高红移极端过程产生的瞬态或部分再电离所贡献的额外光学深度。具体而言，我们探讨了来自单色谱原初黑洞的霍金辐射的影响，保留了约束这些历史的高ℓTT/TE/EE数据，并联合变化再电离红移。我们发现CMB数据并不显著偏好这些额外信号：增强最多为Δτ≃0.008，远低于完全消除中等不一致所需的Δτ≃0.03。物质密度亏损和透镜过剩并未显著缓解：我们解释了原因，将其追溯到再电离红移的补偿以及ℓ>30处残余原初黑洞信号。
decision.translation_warning: 原文中Λcdm中的Λ为希腊字母，在翻译中保留；Δτ中的Δ为希腊字母，保留。
